newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA'S MARCUS SLAMS TRANSNET PENSION MANAGEMENT.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA'S MARCUS SLAMS TRANSNET PENSION MANAGEMENT.

text.p: Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus on Wednesday raised tough questions about the management of the state-owned Transnet road, rail and airline corporation and its pension fund.
Speaking during a heated snap debate in parliament, Marcus called for urgent attention to what she called "anomalies" in the management of the corporation and its pension fund.
Transnet last month reported a 253 million rand loss, down from a 118 million rand profit in the fiscal year to March 1995, blamed mainly on retirement benefits of 1.4 billion rand.
- A fully-pensionable wage settlement 4.5 percent higher than budgeted for, contributing 490 million rand to the pension fund's 3.2 billion rand actuarial deficit.
- Pension payout increases two percent above the assumed 7.5 percent increases, adding 800 million rand to the deficit.
- Almost 4,000 pensioners under 35 years of age and 13,000 more under 49 years old.
- A retirement gratuity of three million rand in addition to a monthly pension of 62,600 rand for recently retired 59-year-old managing director Anton Moolman.
Marcus criticised Transet's renewable 10-year lease of two Boeing 747s from its own pension fund at a rate that would have seen them paid for in a decade.
"Who determines the contract and in whose best interest," she asked.
Marcus urged Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau to redefine the retirement policy of the 40 billion rand corporation.
"This requires a vigorous board of directors, a clearly defined role for the board of trustees of the pension fund... and effective oversight by the minister," she said.
Sigcau said in her response the pension controversy was largely the fault of Moolman's regime and she dismissed criticism of the lack of business experience of the new management team.
"This debate is simply about race and nothing else. Let's get it out of our heads that white is synonymous with competence and that black is otherwise," she said.
